Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issues Concerning the Proper Adjudication of Judicial Review Cases Involving Arbitration

Fa [2013] No. 194

To: All Higher People's Courts of Provinces, Autonomous Regions, and Municipalities Directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

Recently, due to the China International Economic and Trade Arbitration Commission (hereinafter referred to as CIETAC) implementing its revised arbitration rules on May 1, 2012, and the former CIETAC Shanghai Sub-Commission (hereinafter referred to as Shanghai CIETAC) and the former CIETAC South China Sub-Commission (hereinafter referred to as South China CIETAC) changing their names and implementing new arbitration rules, disputes have arisen among certain parties concerning the application of arbitration rules and the authority of the aforementioned arbitration institutions to accept arbitration cases. People's courts in various localities have successively accepted arbitration judicial review cases arising from the aforementioned disputes. To unify the standards of adjudication and ensure that the people's courts correctly hear such cases, notice is hereby given on the relevant issues as follows:

In cases where, as a result of the aforementioned disputes, a party applies for confirmation of the validity of an arbitration agreement, or applies for setting aside or refusing to enforce an arbitral award rendered by CIETAC, Shanghai CIETAC, or South China CIETAC, the people's court, before rendering a ruling, must submit its opinion after deliberation by the judicial committee, and report the matter level by level to the Supreme People's Court. The ruling may only be rendered after receiving a reply from the Supreme People's Court.

September 4, 2013
